title: On the Closed-Form of Flow Matching: Generalization Does Not Arise from Ta

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper writes u^{cond}(x_t,z=x_1,t) = (x1-xt)/(1-t) = (x1-x0)/(1-t). Substituting x_t=(1-t)x0+tx1 gives (x1-xt) = (1-t)(x1-x0), so (x1-xt)/(1-t) simplifies to x1-x0, NOT (x1-x0)/(1-t). This contradicts Algorithm 1 in the same paper, which correctly states 'u^{cond}(x_t, t) = (x_1 - x_t)/(1 - t) = x_1 - x_0' with no extra division by (1-t).

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, 'Taken together, recent work points to a sharp phase transition between memorization and generalization (Yoon et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 2024, unpublished).'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The reference list entry for this work reads 'H. Zhang, J. Zhou, Y. Lu, M. Guo, P. Wang, L. Shen, and Q. Qu. predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, 'Kadkhodaie et al. (2024, anticipated), Kamb and Ganguli (2025, manuscript), Ross et al. (2025, forthcoming) suggested a geometric framework...'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: All three works are listed in the reference list as formally published conference papers (ICLR 2024, ICML 2025, ICLR 2025 respectively), yet the in-text citations label them with inconsistent and fabricated status annotations ('anticipated', 'manuscript', 'forthcoming') that contradict their actual publication status shown in the bibliography.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2 main text vs. Appendix A.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The main text claims the closed-form formula 'can be generalized to other choices of continuous distribution p_0 (e.g., the uniform distribution; see Appendix A.1)'. However, Appendix A.1's second proof explicitly retains the Gaussian density for p_0 (e.g. using 'p(x_0) = 1/sqrt((2π)^d) exp(-1/2||x_0||^2)') and instead generalizes the conditioning variable z to pairs (x0, x^(i)); it never derives or discusses a uniform p_0 case, contradicting the forward reference.

The appendix states: 'For each "data" subsampling of the dataset, we trained the model for 5·10^4 iterations, with a batch size of 128, i.e., we trained the models for 128 epochs.' This epoch count (5e4 × 128 / 50,000 = 128) is only valid for the full 50,000-sample CIFAR-10 dataset, but the experiment (Figure 2) explicitly varies the training set size from 10 to 10^4 samples; for these subsampled sizes the actual number of epochs would differ enormously (e.g., up to ~640,000 epochs for n=10), making the stated '128 epochs' incorrect for the described experimental design.

The section is titled 'D.5 Figure 4' but the body text repeatedly refers to 'Figures 2 and 3' and '(Figure 3)' instead of Figure 4: 'For experiments involving training on CIFAR-10 (Figures 2 and 3), we rely on...' and 'For CelebA 64 × 64 (Figure 3), we rely on the training script of pnpflow library'. These figure references are inconsistent with the stated section topic and with earlier appendix sections (D.3 already covers Figure 2, D.4 already covers Figure 3).

Appendix C begins with 'We present below the results for the MNIST dataset,' yet both Table 1 and Table 2 are captioned 'FID FMNIST', creating a direct contradiction about which dataset the reported results pertain to.

Proposition 2(ii) proves an exact equality: 'the minimizer of Equation (7) equals the optimal velocity field' (Eq. 10), implying exact unbiasedness. Yet the subsequent text directly contradicts this proven result: 'Self-normalized importance-sampling estimators of û⋆ are typically biased... this does not guarantee unbiasedness in the standard Monte Carlo sense... The theoretical claims therefore approximate unbiasedness within empirical tolerance.' This hedging directly undermines and contradicts the exact mathematical claim just proven in Proposition 2.

The text admits 'The vertical axis is capped at 20, obscuring the full range of distances; error bars indicating standard deviation across runs are omitted.' Yet immediately after, the paper claims 'the increase in average distance is modest and within margin of error, thus providing only weak evidence that the model generalizes better' — a statistical claim about margin of error that cannot be substantiated given the explicit absence of error bars/standard deviations.

The caption states 'Following û* until τ ≥ 0.3 yields a model that is not able to generalize,' but the body text describing the same figure uses different thresholds: 'For τ ≤ 0.2, the hybrid model remains as creative as u_θ... For τ > 0.2, the LPIPS distance starts dropping... as soon as τ ≥ 0.4, the sample generated by the hybrid model is almost the same as the one obtained with û*(τ=1).'
